title: Severe Cyclone Murasu 200 km from Chennai, set to cross Andhra coast near Ongole late Monday
dek: The storm strengthened into a severe cyclonic storm overnight and is due to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur from late Monday, with gusts of up to 120 kmph and a surge of up to 1.5 m. Five Andhra districts are on red alert; Bengal faces only light rain.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Murasu has strengthened into a severe cyclonic storm and was centred about 200 km east-northeast of Chennai and 260 km southeast of Ongole at 5.30 am IST on Monday, moving west-northwest at about 25 kmph, according to the India Meteorological Department's (IMD) morning bulletin as reported by OMMCOM News. It is forecast to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between about 11.30 pm on Monday, 2 November, and 4 am on Tuesday, 3 November, with sustained winds of 100 to 110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph.

The IMD has warned of a storm surge of 1 to 1.5 metres above the astronomical tide in low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh at landfall, with Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts most at risk. Five Andhra districts are under a red alert for extremely heavy rain. Murasu, a Tamil word for a drum, is the second cyclone to threaten the Andhra coast in a week, after Cyclone Arnab. There is still no weather warning for West Bengal, but the distant warning signal at the Kolkata and Haldia ports has been raised.

## Latest bulletin

The storm moved quickly towards the coast overnight. At 2.30 am it was near latitude 13.6°N, longitude 82.5°E, about 260 km east-northeast of Chennai, 290 km east-southeast of Nellore and 330 km southeast of Ongole, the IMD said, according to Deccan Chronicle and Sakshi Post. Three hours later it was near 13.9°N, 81.8°E, about 210 km east-southeast of Nellore and 220 km east-southeast of Kavali, OMMCOM News reported, citing the 5.30 am bulletin. The Week reported that the IMD expects it may intensify further, into a very severe cyclonic storm, before landfall; other reports of the same bulletins describe it as a severe cyclonic storm at landfall. Readers should follow the IMD's next bulletins for the final figures.

A red cyclone warning, the last of the IMD's four stages, is in force for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining north Tamil Nadu coasts, according to OMMCOM. Red alerts for extremely heavy rain cover Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam and Nellore districts, Sakshi Post reported, citing the IMD. East and West Godavari, Eluru, NTR, Palnadu, Tirupati and Chittoor are on orange alert, and six more districts, including Kakinada, Konaseema and Kadapa, on yellow. In neighbouring Telangana, Khammam, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Mahabubnagar, Nagarkurnool and Wanaparthy are on orange alert for heavy rain.

The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority, in figures reported by South First on Sunday, expects the storm to cross near Bapatla on Tuesday morning, which lies within the stretch named by the IMD. It forecast district-average rain on Tuesday of about 179 mm in Eluru, 163 mm in Krishna, 161 mm in NTR and 147 mm in West Godavari, and warned of heavy inflows into the Budameru.

After landfall the storm is forecast to weaken quickly to a deep depression by Tuesday evening and a depression by Wednesday morning as it moves north over Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, according to the IMD Kolkata bulletin issued at 10 pm on Sunday.

Gale winds of 80-90 kmph, gusting to 100 kmph, are expected along and off the Andhra coast from Monday evening, rising to 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph, from Monday midnight until Tuesday noon. Fishing is suspended along the Andhra coast until Wednesday afternoon. The IMD has warned of local flooding, disruption to road and rail traffic, damage to kutcha houses, uprooted trees and damage to plantations, and asked authorities to move people out of vulnerable coastal settlements.

## Tamil Nadu

The storm's outer bands are bringing rain to northern Tamil Nadu. Schools and colleges in Chennai and Tiruvallur are closed on Monday, Sakshi Post reported. The IMD forecast heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Chennai and Tiruvallur on Monday, and heavy rain in Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Ranipet and Vellore, easing on Tuesday as the storm moves north, The Week reported. Winds of 60-70 kmph are likely along the north Tamil Nadu and Puducherry coast from Monday evening.

## Andhra Pradesh prepares

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu cancelled a visit to Delhi planned for Monday because of the cyclone, his office said on X on Sunday afternoon. The state health department said on Sunday it had set up 1,688 medical teams, 116 relief camps and 13,165 emergency beds, and readied 733 ambulances and 721 mobile medical units, South First reported. It had identified 6,870 pregnant women due to give birth between 1 and 10 November, and 493 had already been moved to hospitals.

The disaster management authority's helplines are 112, 1070 and 1800 425 0101. Figures for evacuations and the deployment of national and state disaster response teams in Andhra Pradesh had not been published by early Monday.

## What it means for Bengal

The Kolkata bulletin says there is "at present no weather warning for West Bengal" linked to Murasu, which it is keeping under continuous watch. Distant Warning Signal No. 2 has now been hoisted at the Kolkata and Haldia ports, up from the Distant Cautionary Signal No. 1 hoisted on Saturday, with sectional signals II and IV at Sagar Island. A distant signal warns ships leaving port of a storm far out at sea; it does not indicate danger to the port itself.

Light rain or thundershowers are likely in south Bengal on Monday and Tuesday, with light to moderate rain at one or two places in North 24 Parganas, Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly and the Midnapore districts on 3 November, and dry weather from 4 November, the bulletin said.

There is no fishing warning for the Bengal coast, but the IMD has advised Bengal's fishermen not to go towards the west-central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal or the south Odisha coast from 2 to 4 November.

## Odisha braces again

Southern Odisha is still recovering from Cyclone Arnab. The IMD expects squally winds of 40-50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, along the south Odisha coast from Monday evening, rising to 50-60 kmph on Tuesday. IMD Bhubaneswar has issued an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rain in Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati and Ganjam on 3 and 4 November, Argus reported. Odisha's disaster management minister, Suresh Pujari, said the state had kept the arrangements made for Arnab in place and upgraded its preparations, The Week reported. In Rayagada, all 11 fire station teams have been deployed and earthmovers stationed on two ghat sections of National Highway 326, Deccan Chronicle reported. In Ganjam, NDRF and Odisha disaster response teams have been stationed in sensitive areas, according to Pragativadi.

## What happens next

The IMD expects Murasu to reach the coast late on Monday night, with the strongest winds from around midnight until Tuesday noon. Ports and fishermen along the Andhra, Tamil Nadu and Odisha coasts should follow the IMD's district and port warnings, which will be revised as the storm nears land. The Kolkata centre said its next update for Bengal would be issued on Monday.

## Key numbers

- Landfall: south Andhra coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole, between about 11.30 pm on 2 November and 4 am on 3 November
- Peak forecast wind: 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph
- Storm surge: 1-1.5 m above astronomical tide in low-lying south coastal Andhra Pradesh
- Distance from Chennai: about 420 km at 5.30 pm Sunday; about 260 km at 2.30 am Monday; about 200 km at 5.30 am Monday
- Red alert districts: Krishna, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Nellore
- Bengal: no warning; Distant Warning Signal No. 2 at Kolkata and Haldia ports
